**STEP 1 – Scene:** A single short piece of boiled corn on the cob, standing upright (cut end facing the camera), on an otherwise empty plate.

**STEP 2 – Vessel:** A square white plate with rounded corners, about 23 cm across. Its area is roughly 23 × 23 ≈ 500 cm² (slightly less because of the rounded corners).

**STEP 3 – Items:** One piece of corn on the cob, with yellow kernels around a pale cob. No visible butter, oil or sauce.

**STEP 4 – Area:** The corn's footprint is about 6.3 cm in diameter, so π × 3.15² ≈ 31 cm². That is about 6% of the plate area, and it is the only food, so total coverage is about 6%.

**STEP 5 – Volume:** The piece stands upright, and its height is estimated at about 4.5 cm. 31 cm² × 4.5 cm ≈ 140 ml gross volume.

**STEP 6 – Grams:** Corn on the cob is a dense solid but has small gaps between kernels, so I use a bulk density of about 0.7. 140 ml × 0.7 ≈ 98 g, including the cob.

**STEP 7 – Energy:** Boiled corn kernels have about 96 kcal per 100 g. The inedible cob is about 35–40% of the weight, so the whole piece works out to about 65 kcal per 100 g. 98 g × 0.65 ≈ 64 kcal.

**STEP 8 – Sanity check:** A third of an ear of corn would plausibly weigh about 80–110 g with the cob and provide about 55–70 kcal. The estimate falls in that range, so it is reasonable.
